name: Avenue Supermarts Ltd
title: Avenue Supermarts Ltd - 540376 - Transcript Of Conference Call With Analyst/ Institutional Investors

summary.headline: DMart FY26 revenue near INR67,000 crore (+16%), PAT margin ~4.8%; management targets ~15% annual store additions and says SSSG stays at last year's levels.
summary.overview: This was DMart's annual analyst call, the first with Anshul Asawa as MD & CEO, covering FY26 results and the outlook for FY27. Management said the fundamentals were intact but flagged higher staff costs for capability build, a slowdown in same-store growth in mature metro stores, and heavy competitive pressure from quick commerce. Avenue E-commerce (DMart Ready) was narrowed to 11 cities after exits from seven cities, with its EBITDA falling about 43% and a net loss of INR307 crore. Management reiterated a roughly 15% internal store-addition target and did not disclose e-commerce KPIs.

financial_highlights.change: Roughly flat; gross margin +16 bps, employee cost +27 bps, other expenses -9 bps
Total debt incl. AS 116 INR2,267 crore
Retail business area ~20.6 million sq ft
Sales +17%; PBT -24%; net loss INR307 crore

segments.name: Avenue Supermarts (standalone DMart stores)
segments.commentary: Sales +~16% with gross margin up 16 bps to within the 14-15% range; employee cost up ~33% in standalone financials including wage code impact. Entered five new states in FY26.

segments.name: Avenue E-commerce (DMart Ready)
segments.commentary: Sales +17% but EBITDA down ~43% and net loss INR307 crore. Exited seven quick-commerce cities; now focused on 11 cities, with 165 pickup points cited. Contract labour cost +24% and transport +34%.

segments.name: Avenue Food Plaza (fast/ready food)
segments.commentary: Sales +~35.5%; returned to profit with PAT margin ~9% after prior-year losses from expansion.

guidance_outlook: Internal store-addition benchmark ~15% of store base annually; could run a few points higher or lower depending on real estate timing.
Same-store growth expected to hover around last financial year's level (~7.5-8%) for FY27 for older stores; no sharp increase expected, all else equal.
Long-term North Star: ~15% gross margin and ~5% net margin; no intention to expand margin at the cost of customer proposition.
Expect efficiency gains in AEL from consolidation to 11 cities in FY27 onwards, per AEL CEO.
Staff cost built ahead of volume growth; management says it is hard to say if the build-up has ended.
Plans to invest in ERP and wider technology upgrades; management expects only marginal near-term margin impact.
capex_capacity: FY26 store additions: 85, with 15 on long-term lease; 68 stores in total now on lease out of 500+.
Land-to-store conversion takes 2-3 years depending on store configuration; pipeline of projects covers the next 2-3 years.
Debt: CP outstanding ~INR800 crore; INR1,000 crore NCD approved, may take total borrowing to ~INR2,000 crore by year-end, mainly to fund capex and reduce cost of debt.
Warehouses added in FY26 raised inventory days to 33.2.
demand_pricing: Quick commerce competition intensifying in dense metros (Mumbai, Bangalore, Hyderabad) where mature stores are saturated; management cites capacity, saturation, high throughput and competition as reasons for slower metro SSSG.
Management says FMCG vendors are not shifting attention away from DMart; many are doubling down.
Management says monthly/bulk shopping in metros is stable and strong, with good traction in Tier 1 and Tier 2 cities; newer Tier 2/3 stores are doing better than older metro stores.
Pricing follows vendor pass-through; no pricing guidance given.
Quarterly growth was 13% (Dec-25 quarter, deflation in staples), 19% (Mar-26 quarter, panic buying), and 15% (Jun-26 quarter).

qa_highlights.question: Will SSSG recover to double-digit levels given quick-commerce and maturity pressures in metros?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said SSSG is likely to hover around the current range (~7-8%) and not rise considerably, especially for older stores; new stores are opened nearby to reduce pressure on existing stores.

qa_highlights.question: Why is the 15% store-addition target conservative and can it go to 100-150 stores a year?
qa_highlights.answer: Internal target is ~15%; capital and people are not constraints, and land acquisition, permissions and build time (2-3 years) are. Management said 100-150 stores is not a reasonable number at about 500 stores currently.

qa_highlights.question: What is the economics of leasing versus owning stores?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to share lease vs owned economics; said both models work. 68 stores are on long leases and 15 of the 85 stores added in FY26 were leased. Niladri said PBT is a fair measure of lease impact.

qa_highlights.question: Why did the mix of AEL get cut to 11 cities and why not experiment with faster delivery?
qa_highlights.answer: Seven cities were exited because their contribution was minimal. Management said it will not pursue immediate delivery; it will prove the six-hour slotted model in 11 cities first because losses had grown with expansion.

qa_highlights.question: What is driving the rise in employee costs and why are contractual headcounts lower?
qa_highlights.answer: Permanent headcount rose ~4,000 (75-80% of additions are store-management cohorts). Frontline staff are non-permanent; productivity and mechanisation held down non-permanent headcount. Wage code from December 2025 also added costs.

qa_highlights.question: Will the company add non-metro growth via quick commerce given Flipkart and Blinkit expansion?
qa_highlights.answer: Management does not see a risk of LFL falling below 5%; it sees organised retail still under-penetrated in smaller towns and has no point of view on QC adoption outside top cities.

risks_watch: Continued SSSG slowdown in mature metro stores (~7-8% range expected) as quick commerce and new nearby stores take share.
AEL profitability: EBITDA down ~43% with net loss INR307 crore; watch whether consolidation to 11 cities improves throughput and transport/labour costs in FY27.
Rising staff costs (employee cost +27 bps of sales, standalone employee expense up ~33%) with wage code impact and capability build.
Lower return ratios (ROE ~13.5%, ROCE ~17.1%) and rising debt to fund expansion; NCD plan of INR1,000 crore.
Store-addition pace (85 in FY26 vs ~15% target) depends on land and lease availability; slower ramp in new Tier 2/3 stores.
Management declined to disclose DMart Ready KPIs, store-level margins, lease economics, land value, and category-level data.
summary.management_tone: Confident on the core store model and value proposition, but cautious on e-commerce profitability and store growth pace. Management was evasive on specific metrics (e-commerce KPIs, lease economics, land value, pricing outlook), deferring with 'we don't disclose' responses.
key_quotes: The model that this business has of providing everyday low price through an everyday low-cost operation isn't just a strategy, but it also has become its moat and will continue to protect us for years to come.
So we do want to prove that this way of working is sustainable in these 11 cities first, and so we are channeling all our attention and resources in AEL towards this goal.
And so therefore, 15% kind of a gross margin and let's say around a 5% kind of a net margin should be the North Star for this business even in the future.

adds.what: ~15% of store base added annually (85 stores opened in FY26; 15 on lease)

growth.why: Management held a ~15% annual store-addition benchmark and same-store growth near 7.5-8% for FY27, backed by a land-to-store pipeline covering 2-3 years and 85 stores opened in FY26, though no explicit FY27 store count or capex figure was given; the Q1 revenue growth of 15% supports a growth tilt.

mgmt.note: Anshul Asawa is the new MD & CEO; he is backing the ~15% annual store-addition benchmark and same-store growth held near 7.5-8% for FY27.
initiatives: Expand store count in new states and Tier 2/3 cities
